note.question: How does inventory considerations” affect comment on “salesforce compensation?
note.overview: In this rejoinder, we address the concern about equilibrium existence in our previous work published in 2013. By making the simple adjustment of discretizing inventory ordering amounts to prevent inventory orders in arbitrarily small increments, we show that the results from that paper hold, thus maintaining the robustness of the insights obtained. This paper was accepted by Jeannette Song, operations management.

By making the simple adjustment of discretizing inventory ordering amounts to prevent inventory orders in arbitrarily small increments, we show that the results from that paper hold, thus maintaining the robustness of the insights obtained. This paper was accepted by Jeannette Song, operations management.

source.quote: Thus, the basic economic insight that the firm orders more inventory to improve the observability of agent effort, which is the main point of Dai and Jerath (2013), continues to hold.
Thus, the basic economic insight that the firm orders more inventory to improve the observability of agent effort, which is the main point of Dai and Jerath (2013), continues to hold.

If actual demand exceeds inventory, demand beyond inventory is unobservable, leading to “demand censoring.” We find that this leads the firm to “overcompensate” the salesperson because of limited observability.
Thus, the basic economic insight that the firm orders more inventory to improve the observability of agent effort, which is the main point of Dai and Jerath (2013), continues to hold.
